name: HerdDB
tagline: JVM-embeddable distributed SQL database replicated with Apache BookKeeper and ZooKeeper.
description: HerdDB is a distributed SQL database written in Java by the Italian company Diennea. Each JVM can embed a node and read local data without a network hop, or run as a standalone server reached over JDBC. Internally it is a key-value store with a SQL layer planned by Apache Calcite; tables are grouped into tablespaces, and each tablespace has one leader and a set of replicas whose write-ahead log is replicated through Apache BookKeeper, with ZooKeeper handling metadata and leader election, so no shared storage is needed. Transactions use read-committed isolation and may span tables only within one tablespace. It is tuned for fast writes and primary-key access. Releases have slowed to occasional maintenance; 0.29.0 shipped in March 2024.
statusNote: Last release 0.29.0 (March 2024); recent commits are build and dependency upkeep only.

scale.notes: Data is partitioned by tablespace, each led by one node with replicas; transactions cannot span tablespaces.

strengths: Runs embedded in the application JVM or as a cluster of servers
Replication on BookKeeper and ZooKeeper without shared storage
weaknesses: Read-committed isolation only; no serializable transactions
Transactions and subqueries limited to a single tablespace
Small community and slow release cadence
Requires operating ZooKeeper and BookKeeper for replication
useCases: Embedded replicated SQL store inside Java services
Metadata and configuration storage for JVM platforms
